children: – Jabal Akhdar welcomed 101,608 visitors in the first half of 2026, marking a 13.2% increase over the same period last year, highlighting the growing appeal of one of Oman’s leading mountain destinations.

The rise comes as Jabal Akhdar prepares to become the Gulf Tourism Capital for 2027, with authorities working to strengthen infrastructure, develop new tourism experiences and expand investment opportunities for businesses and local communities.
Data from the National Centre for Statistics and Information (NCSI) showed that visitor numbers increased from 89,780 in the first half of 2025 to 101,608 in H1 2026.
The growth coincided with increased tourism activity, including the annual Rose Spring Festival, which draws visitors to experience Jabal Akhdar’s agricultural traditions and seasonal rose harvest.
He said these businesses could benefit from increased tourism activity in accommodation, hospitality, restaurants, cafes, transport and tourism experiences.

Agriculture remains central to the area’s economic and tourism identity, with pomegranates, olives, saffron, roses, aromatic plants and other fruits among its key products. There are 14 agricultural investment projects covering approximately 166 feddans, with a combined investment value of RO3.5mn.
The wilayat is also witnessing development and service projects worth more than RO5.7mn, including road upgrades, public facilities and improvements to health and administrative services.

Among the ongoing works are consultancy services for the design of a dual carriageway and the upgrading of the 5km entrance to Jabal Akhdar, which is 90% complete. Planning for an investment park focused on agricultural and handicraft products, tourism events and programmes is 50% complete.

A major project is Al Jabal Al Aali , with an estimated investment value of RO1.2bn. Covering 11.8sqkm at an altitude of about 2,400m, it is planned to accommodate around 10,000 residents, with more than 2,500 residential units and 2,000 hotel rooms, alongside tourism, leisure, cultural and sports facilities.

title: ZAWYA: Oman: Jabal Akhdar tourism rises 13.2% in H1
